title: Official MCP stdio adapter
description: Objective: expose generated safe commands and queries through the official stable MCP TypeScript SDK over stdio. Deliverable: packages/mcp stdio modules and protocol fixtures. NOT in scope: lifecycle logic, custom WebSocket MCP, or IDE-specific behavior. Hard dependency: stable generated daemon contracts. Owned paths: packages/mcp/src/stdio/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/mcp test.
definitionOfDone: Tool schemas are generated and bounded; authentication/capability checks match HTTP.
Command IDs, stable errors, truth, cursors, and recovery commands preserve parity.
Malformed, oversized, stale, and disconnected clients fail closed.
taskRails: Portability consumes frozen daemon/core contracts; adapters cannot fork lifecycle or authority semantics.
Official MCP stdio and Streamable HTTP only; no custom MCP-over-WebSocket dialect.
Unsupported OS/provider/import facts remain typed UNSUPPORTED or UNKNOWN, never guessed.
IDE adapters are thin optional shells for the standalone control room. Keep files below 400 lines and use explicit owned paths.

implementationPlan.description: Scaffold @moe/mcp. package.json: { name: "@moe/mcp", version: "0.0.0", private: true, type: "module", exports: { ".": "./src/index.ts" } (repo convention — scheduler package-boundary test asserts this shape; future Streamable HTTP + daemon import through it), dependencies: { "@moe/contracts": "workspace:*", "@modelcontextprotocol/sdk": "1.30.0" (exact — saveExact; FIRST external runtime dependency: ~93 transitive lockfile entries (express 5, hono, jose, ajv...), zero build scripts, no pnpm-11 approval needed — empirically probed; record resolved tree size in step note) }, scripts: { typecheck: "tsc --project tsconfig.json", test: "vitest run --root ../.. packages/mcp/src" }. NO zod dependency — the plan deliberately uses the SDK's LOW-LEVEL Server class (step 4), not McpServer, whose inputSchema is zod-only. tsconfig.json mirrors packages/contracts EXCEPT: tsBuildInfoFile "../../node_modules/.cache/mcp.tsbuildinfo" AND "skipLibCheck": true — MANDATORY: SDK d.ts references HeadersInit which @types/node 24.13.3 does not declare globally; without skipLibCheck `pnpm --filter @moe/mcp typecheck` fails with TS2304 (empirically proven with repo toolchain). src/index.ts placeholder. Run `pnpm install`. Lockfile state verified clean at planning time (no uncommitted foreign importers); re-verify at commit time per the standing ordering rule. Placement note for step note: AGENTS.md reserves adapters/* for integration boundaries but governor granted packages/mcp — record the tension, do not relocate. Do NOT run the package test script before the first test file exists (passWithNoTests:false).

implementationPlan.description: TDD red — src/stdio/stdio-schemas.test.ts. Assert on the generated tool surface: (1) determinism — two generation runs byte-identical; (2) coverage — exactly one tool per RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS entry + one per RUNTIME_QUERY_KINDS entry, no extras; (3) NAME MAPPING — kinds contain dots (goal.create) which common client/LLM tool-name grammars ([a-zA-Z0-9_-]) reject: deterministic bijective label mapping '.' -> '_' generated alongside schemas; test asserts bijectivity (no two kinds collide after mapping) and round-trip label->kind->label identity; the VERBATIM kind is carried in each schema's description and in the envelope commandKind (design 1009 identity lives in the envelope, not the transport label); (4) CREDENTIAL EXCLUSION (security-critical): no generated input schema contains sessionCredential, requestDigest, or any credential-bearing property — tool inputs are the envelope key sets MINUS adapter-supplied fields; MCP clients log tool args, and design 1139/1141 forbid credentials in logs; (5) bounds — every string property carries maxLength derived from input-limits constants; payload is a bounded OPAQUE object (envelope-shaped schemas are an EXPLICIT interim: design 982's one-source-schema generation pipeline is M3 scope; record the follow-up to re-point the generator at M3's per-command surface when it lands). Confirm RED.

implementationPlan.description: Green — src/stdio/stdio-tool-schemas.ts + src/stdio/stdio-dispatch-port.ts (each target <=250). stdio-tool-schemas.ts: mechanical generation from RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS/RUNTIME_QUERY_KINDS + envelope required/optional key sets MINUS adapter-supplied fields (sessionCredential always; requestDigest — adapter computes it over the canonical payload bytes, clients never supply it); plain frozen JSON-Schema data objects (NOT zod — low-level Server serves them verbatim); bijective name mapping exported. stdio-dispatch-port.ts: typed injected port — { authenticate(credential: string, toolKind: string): frozen auth result; dispatchCommandBytes(bytes: Uint8Array): Uint8Array; dispatchQueryBytes(bytes: Uint8Array): Uint8Array } — RAW BYTES both directions (pass-through parity: any parse->re-stringify normalizes escapes/number format/key order and corrupts digest-bound fields and opaque cursors); port contract doc pins the CALL-SEQUENCE OBLIGATION: bounded decode -> authenticate -> dispatch; auth failure short-circuits with ZERO dispatch calls. Also src/dispatch-conformance.ts (scaffold grant, OUTSIDE stdio/ so the Streamable HTTP task imports the SAME suite): transport-agnostic executable conformance fixtures — call-recording fake port asserting the sequence obligation, golden request/response fixtures, and the FULL error-mapping table iterating EVERY RUNTIME_ERROR_CODES entry against lookupRuntimeError(code).transport.mcpCode (design 1130 parity becomes a shared executable gate, not prose; design 1062 registry fixes the mapping). Boundary-scan rule: no '@moe/scheduler/' or 'scheduler/src/' substrings anywhere in packages/mcp sources. Schema tests green.
implementationPlan.note: Reopen audit: generated tool schemas, raw-byte dispatch port (including advisory AbortSignal amendment), and transport-agnostic conformance suite remain committed and explicitly verified GOOD by QA. No production rebuild or drift.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red then green — src/stdio/stdio-server.test.ts + src/stdio/stdio-server.ts. Server: LOW-LEVEL SDK Server class + setRequestHandler for ListTools/CallTool (NOT McpServer — its inputSchema is zod-only; low-level serves the generated JSON Schema objects verbatim, zero zod). Per CallTool: map label->kind; build the envelope object by INJECTING the bootstrap credential (read ONCE from the spawning process env per design 1141, held in closure, never logged, never echoed in errors) + computing requestDigest over canonical payload bytes; serialize to bytes; decodeRuntimeCommandEnvelopeBytes/decodeRuntimeQueryEnvelopeBytes (fail closed on malformed/oversized with the decoder's stable RuntimeError); port.authenticate (fail short-circuits, zero dispatch); port.dispatch*Bytes; emit daemon bytes VERBATIM as a single UTF-8 text content block — NO outputSchema/structuredContent (SDK would force re-serialization), NEVER re-parse (command IDs, truth classes, cursors, nextAllowedCommands, recovery commands survive byte-identical). Error routing: ADAPTER-detected failures (malformed, oversized, unknown tool, auth-reject) -> JSON-RPC McpError with registry mcpCode AND the full bounded RuntimeError (code, retryability, redacted details, recovery set — design 1058) in error.data; DAEMON dispatch rejections -> daemon error bytes passed through verbatim in the result content so the LLM client sees recovery commands. Disconnect mid-dispatch: discard outcome, fabricate nothing (idempotency = daemon ledger's job). Tests via SDK InMemoryTransport client<->server with fake recording port: happy command/query roundtrip (fixture daemon bytes survive byte-identical in result.content[0].text — REAL byte-identity even over InMemoryTransport because bytes ride as an opaque string), unknown tool, auth-reject (zero dispatch calls recorded), oversized args, error-mapping spot checks + run the SHARED dispatch-conformance suite; MALFORMED-BYTES CAVEAT: InMemoryTransport passes JSON-RPC objects by reference — malformed wire bytes are unrepresentable in a protocol roundtrip, so the decoder's malformed branch is tested by invoking the registered CallTool handler/decoder DIRECTLY with hostile bytes (state this in the test file header; do not pretend the roundtrip covers it). Both suites green.

comments.content: Architect amendment for step 3 (stdio-dispatch-port.ts), from planning the dependent Streamable HTTP task: give both dispatch methods an OPTIONAL AbortSignal — dispatchCommandBytes(bytes: Uint8Array, signal?: AbortSignal): Uint8Array and dispatchQueryBytes(bytes: Uint8Array, signal?: AbortSignal): Uint8Array. Rationale: the SDK surfaces client cancellation (notifications/cancelled) as extra.signal on the request-handler extra for BOTH transports (shared/protocol.js registers a per-request AbortController and passes signal into the handler extra); the HTTP task owns only packages/mcp/src/http/** and cannot extend the port later without touching your file. stdio-server.ts should pass extra.signal through when invoking the port; ignoring it remains legal for port implementations (the SDK already suppresses the response of a cancelled request). Document the param as advisory cancellation, never an authority change. One-line type addition; no behavior change required in your tests beyond accepting the extra parameter.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) McpServer high-level API — REJECTED: its inputSchema type is zod-only (sdk zod-compat.d.ts AnySchema); feeding generated JSON Schema requires either a zod dependency (new external dep, drift between generated schema and zod re-derivation) or is impossible; LOW-LEVEL Server + setRequestHandler serves the frozen generated JSON Schema objects verbatim with zero zod. (2) Verbatim dotted tool names (goal.create) — REJECTED as sole mechanism: common client tool-name grammars reject dots; deterministic bijective '.'->'_' label mapping with bijectivity test; envelope commandKind carries the verbatim identity (design 1009). (3) Credential as tool argument — REJECTED (security): MCP clients log tool args; design 1139/1141. Tool schemas = envelope keys MINUS sessionCredential (+ requestDigest, adapter-computed); server injects the spawn-env bootstrap credential before decode. (4) Parity-by-prose (shared port 'by construction') — REJECTED as DoD1 evidence: shipped instead as an executable transport-agnostic conformance suite (src/dispatch-conformance.ts) with call-sequence obligation + full registry error-mapping table; the Streamable HTTP sibling imports the same suite. (5) Blocking on M3 like the Codex task — REJECTED decisively: every surface this adapter INTERPRETS is landed/frozen/versioned (kind vocabularies, exact-key bounded envelope decoders, error registry with per-code mcpCode); everything else is opaque bytes behind the injected DispatchPort; Codex's dependency existed in NO form. Interim honesty: tool schemas are envelope-shaped (bounded opaque payload) until M3's one-source-schema pipeline lands — recorded follow-up. Verified by 2-agent workflow; 2 BLOCKERs + 5 RISKs folded in.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: SDK 1.30.0 empirical probes (repo-exact toolchain): (a) tsc FAILS without skipLibCheck — SDK d.ts uses HeadersInit, absent from @types/node 24.13.3 globals (TS2304); skipLibCheck:true in packages/mcp/tsconfig.json fixes it (proven). (b) pnpm install succeeds with ONLY the SDK declared — zod is dual-listed dep+peer and self-satisfies; ~93 transitive entries (express 5, hono, jose, ajv...), zero build scripts, no pnpm-11 onlyBuiltDependencies approval. (c) InMemoryTransport passes JSON-RPC objects BY REFERENCE (no serialization) — malformed wire bytes unrepresentable via roundtrip; byte-identity parity IS testable by riding daemon bytes as an opaque string in result.content[0].text; decoder's malformed branch tested by direct handler invocation. Registry transport bindings landed: mcpCode -32001..-32007 per category (runtime-error-registry.ts:42-53). Envelope decoders REQUIRE sessionCredential non-empty + requestDigest hex64 (runtime-envelope.ts:56-66,143-147) — hence adapter-side injection. No repo dependency-allowlist test exists (hygiene task owned only .gitignore + docs). exports {".": "./src/index.ts"} is the asserted package-root convention. AGENTS.md reserves adapters/* — governor granted packages/mcp; tension recorded, not relocated.
planningNotes.risks: (1) Credential leakage is the top security risk: exactly one process.env read site, closure-held, never in schemas/logs/errors/ListTools; step-5 grep + step-6 red-team enforce. (2) Byte fidelity: ANY parse->re-stringify of daemon bytes corrupts digest-bound fields/opaque cursors — port is bytes-in/bytes-out, content block is opaque text, no outputSchema/structuredContent. (3) SDK upgrade drift: 1.30.0 exact-pinned; skipLibCheck hides SDK type breakage — acceptable, scoped to this package. (4) Envelope-shaped schemas are interim (M3 gap) — explicitly documented, follow-up recorded; QA should not read them as the final generated surface. (5) Malformed-bytes test honesty: state the direct-invocation caveat in the test header or the fixture silently tests the SDK's own -32602 path. (6) First external dep: ~93 lockfile entries land in one commit — lockfile ordering rule applies (every importer resolves to committed package.json; planning/ sources are untracked foreign work with no importer today). (7) Boundary scan covers packages/mcp — no forbidden substrings anywhere including comments.

issues.description: MUTATION A, SURVIVED (48/48 green): in buildCommandEnvelopeBytes move ONLY `commandKind: kind` above `...args`. Client invokes tool `goal_create` with arguments.commandKind='goal.close'. callTool resolves entry from the LABEL, so entry.kind stays 'goal.create' and decodeAndDispatch authenticates the capability for goal.create, while the dispatched bytes carry 'goal.close' (accepted by isCommandKind, runtime-envelope.ts:142). Daemon executes a command the client was never authorized for.

MUTATION B, KILLED (contrast): moving all FOUR adapter fields above `...args` fails exactly one test. sessionCredential and requestDigest ARE locked; commandKind and schemaVersion are not. Schema tests do not close this — stdio-schemas.test.ts:124 asserts commandKind is absent from the static inputSchema, a claim about what is ADVERTISED, not what a hostile client can SEND. The SDK enforces nothing server-side.

FIX (command surface): assert on the decoded port.dispatched[0] envelope that a client-supplied commandKind (a DIFFERENT valid kind) and a wrong schemaVersion are both overwritten with the label-derived kind and RUNTIME_COMMAND_ENVELOPE_VERSION. Drive it off the exported ADAPTER_SUPPLIED_COMMAND_FIELDS so a field added there later is covered automatically. Then re-run mutation A and confirm it dies.

buildQueryEnvelopeBytes has NO override test at all: queryKind, schemaVersion and sessionCredential are all unlocked on the query surface. The existing smuggle test exercises only the command surface. Add the query counterpart driven off ADAPTER_SUPPLIED_QUERY_FIELDS, asserting each is overwritten with the adapter value.

'refuses a client attempt to smuggle its own credential or digest' covers 2 of 4 command adapter-supplied fields and 0 of 3 query fields, which is exactly why mutation A survives it. Broaden it or add a sibling covering the declared adapter-supplied sets on BOTH surfaces. Your handoff memory states this behaviour is tested; it is half tested.

NON-BLOCKING, no action this reopen. Disconnected-client-mid-dispatch has no test. I verified the claim myself by construction rather than on trust: callTool, decodeAndDispatch and the CallTool handler contain no `await`, so there is no interleaving point at which a disconnect could fabricate or half-authorize an outcome. The design argument holds. Leave it.

NON-BLOCKING, no action. requestDigest = sha256 over JSON.stringify(payload ?? null). Contracts constrain it only to hex64 (runtime-envelope.ts:147) and @moe/contracts has no canonical-JSON helper, so nothing is violated. But this adapter is now the de facto definition, and a daemon that later canonicalises will reject every command. Flag to the architect for a shared helper; do not invent one here.

NON-BLOCKING, no action. 272 lines is over the 250 soft target, under the 400 hard rail; fixture module, fine. Also agreed and correctly left untouched: SDK ErrorCode.RequestTimeout -32001 collides with the frozen registry's UNAUTHENTICATED binding, so clients must read error.data.code. Architect's call.
